claims.quote: methyl-CpG binding protein 2 (MeCP2) is lactylated at lysine 210 (K210)

claims.object_text: transcriptional activation of glycolytic/inflammatory genes, especially hexokinase 2 (HK2)
claims.quote: enhancing its transcriptional activation of glycolytic/inflammatory genes, especially hexokinase 2 (HK2).

claims.object_text: impairs mitochondrial respiration; dysregulates mTOR/AMPK signaling; sustains neuroinflammation
claims.quote: Lactylated MeCP2 impairs mitochondrial respiration, disrupts metabolic signaling (leading to dysregulated activation of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR)/AMPK pathway), and sustains neuroinflammation.

claims.object_text: Genetic ablation of MeCP2-K210 lactylation via K210R mutation
claims.quote: Genetic ablation of MeCP2-K210 lactylation (via K210R mutation), pharmacological inhibition of lactyltransferase p300, or HK2 inhibition with lonidamine restores mitochondrial function, attenuates neuroinflammation, and improves neurofunctional recovery.

claims.object_text: MeCP2-K210 lactylation drives microglial activation via the HK2/mTOR axis
claims.quote: The findings establish MeCP2-K210 lactylation as a critical metabolic-epigenetic switch driving microglial activation via the HK2/mTOR axis, identifying a therapeutic target for postischemic neuroinflammation.
